intent:
Write a ~350-word grounded explainer on how active noise cancellation in headphones works and where it falls short in everyday use. Pull the technical definition from English Wikipedia (__WIKIPEDIA__), at least one real user experience thread from Postmill (__REDDIT__), and at least one concrete product page for an ANC headphone from the One Stop Market store (__SHOPPING__). Cite every factual claim as a markdown [label](url) link to sandbox-local pages you actually opened. The report must explain (1) the destructive-interference mechanism, (2) at least one concrete limitation users hit (wind, sudden voices, fit, high-frequency noise), and (3) how a forum user's lived experience or a product's advertised spec lines up with or diverges from the textbook description. Answer starts with the report in Markdown; no chain-of-thought.

[Modality demonstrator: this task declares the rag_search local dense+hybrid (BM25+embedding) retriever over the fixed corpus; the reward is modality-agnostic, so a chunk surfaced by rag_search is credited identically to a fetched page.]
